suppress.notes: Vulnerability in Guava if using com.google.common.io.Files.createTempDir. No version exists without this vulnerability, but the function is marked as deprecated in version 30+ We do not use this function in the code so handled as false positive. file name: guava-31.1-jre.jar

Disputed. The vendor's perspective is that this is not a valid vulnerability report, because the steps of constructing a cyclic data structure and trying to serialize it cannot be achieved by an external attacker. file name: jackson-databind-2.15.2.jar
Disputed as it is a user configuration issue and not a problem with Netty. file name: netty-handler-4.1.98.Final.jar

False positive. CVE-2020-29582 was fixed in Kotlin 1.4.21. The NVD CPE matching incorrectly flags kotlin-stdlib 2.0.0+. The vulnerability concerned insecure use of java.io.tmpdir in kotlin.io.path extension functions on Windows.

False positive. CVE-2026-33186 affects gRPC-Go (the Go language implementation), not gRPC-Java. The CVE's vulnerable CPE is cpe:2.3:a:grpc:grpc:*:*:*:*:*:go:*:* (target_sw=go) and the GHSA tracker GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3 lists the affected ecosystem as Go modules. OWASP Dependency-Check matches it against io.grpc:grpc-* (Java) only because the CPE name "grpc:grpc" is shared between the two implementations.
CPE confusion: io.grpc:grpc-protobuf is the gRPC-Java protobuf integration module, not Google's protobuf project. The cpe:/a:protobuf:protobuf identifier is incorrectly matched here.

False positive. CVE-2026-42582 is an unbounded-allocation DoS in the HTTP/3 QPACK decoder (io.netty:netty-codec-http3, QpackDecoder#decodeHuffmanEncodedLiteral), fixed in 4.2.13.Final. The netty-codec-http3 artifact only exists in the 4.2.x line, so the Netty 4.1.x artifacts flagged by OWASP (netty-codec-memcache, netty-codec-mqtt, netty-transport, etc., pulled in transitively via netty-all) are not the vulnerable component. They are matched only on the shared cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty CPE. There is no 4.1.x release that addresses this CVE.

False positive. CVE-2026-42587 is a decompression-bomb DoS in io.netty:netty-codec-http (HttpContentDecompressor ignoring maxAllocation for br/zstd/snappy), fixed in 4.1.133.Final (4.1.x line) and 4.2.13.Final (4.2.x line). NVD's shared cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty range over-matches and still flags 4.1.133+ as vulnerable. This suppression is scoped to netty-codec-http at 4.1.133 and above only, so genuinely vulnerable versions below 4.1.133 are still reported.

False positive. CVE-2026-40984 is a DoS in Micrometer's HTTP server instrumentations (unbounded URI-tag cardinality). Per the Spring advisory (https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-40984/) the affected branches are 1.9.0-1.9.17, 1.13.0-1.13.18, 1.14.0-1.14.15, 1.15.0-1.15.11 and 1.16.0-1.16.5 — the 1.10.x-1.12.x line is NOT affected. micrometer-core 1.10.1 (pinned fleet-wide via postchain) is flagged only because NVD's CPE range over-matches. This suppression is scoped to 1.10.x-1.12.x only, so a future bump into a genuinely affected branch is still reported.

CVE-2026-54515 (CVSS 6.9): case-insensitive deserialization can bypass per-property @JsonIgnoreProperties. Not exploitable in our stack: it requires MapperFeature.ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES to be enabled AND @JsonIgnoreProperties to be used as an ignore boundary on untrusted input. postchain (which pins jackson and propagates it to all consumers via its BOM) enables neither, and does not invoke the jackson API on untrusted input at all (the REST API uses Gson + GTV binary). jackson-databind 2.22.0 is also the latest release and already fixes the rest of the 2026 cluster (CVE-2026-54512/54513/54514/54516/54517/54518); only this one still matches and no fixed release exists yet. Remove once a patched jackson-databind ships.
